For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

- [ ] **Financial invariants**: commission is never paid from conditional rewards; refunds adjust unpaid or reserved commission; negative adjustments travel with withdrawals; no double allocation under contention; ledger and audit append-only.

- [ ] **Public profile view**: only live, consented, approved content of an active partner with current entitlement; no private columns; partner self-takedown.
- [ ] **Exclusivity**: area-tree containment, fail-closed review for unclassified wording, partner requests never evaluated against exclusivity.
- [ ] **Domain allocation and release**: single holder under races; release founder-only, reasoned, audited, permanent; suppression unaffected.
- [ ] **CI workflow**: `postgres-expansion` service, CI-only credentials, skip guard; no new secrets, permissions or deploy steps.
- [ ] **Production deployment triggers**: none in GitHub; confirm no host-side automation.
- [ ] **Rollback**: restore the pre-migration backup; keep all partner flags unset.

## After a permitted merge

Verify the merge commit and its tree on `master`, inspect `master` CI, confirm every protected flag above remains unset in production configuration, and confirm no deployment occurred. Do not activate partner intake, public profiles, withdrawals or rewards. B1 (Operation Empower) must not begin until this is recorded.

# Operation Empower: B1 planning package

**Package status: DRAFT. Nothing in this folder is approved, published or available to partners or clients.**

Operation Empower prepares two partner capabilities for engineering:

- the **Partner Academy**, an optional, voluntary learning area inside the Partner Portal; and
- the **Sales Resource Centre**, an approved-content library and knowledge base that partners search before speaking to a prospect.

This is B1 research, architecture and content design only. It changes no application code, migrations, authentication, CI or production systems. Implementation must not start until B0 ([PR #155](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/155), branch `claude/modest-newton-jo2d95`) is merged. Its readiness record is [B0-MERGE-READINESS.md](../intelligence/B0-MERGE-READINESS.md).

## Contents

| Document | What it holds |
|---|---|
| [PLATFORM-AUDIT.md](PLATFORM-AUDIT.md) | The existing systems Empower reuses, with file references and gaps |
| [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) | Proposed data model, content lifecycle, deterministic search and integration points |
| [SECURITY-MODEL.md](SECURITY-MODEL.md) | Roles, audience separation, publication controls, threats and mitigations |
| [CURRICULUM.md](CURRICULUM.md) | The 13 Academy courses: objectives, modules, lesson outlines, knowledge checks, resources and review requirements |
| [LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md](LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md) | Initial lesson content, courses 1 to 6 (company and services) |
| [LESSONS-PRACTICE.md](LESSONS-PRACTICE.md) | Initial lesson content, courses 7 to 13 (selling, policy and conduct) |
| [resources/README.md](resources/README.md) | The 13 Resource Centre drafts, one file each |
| [KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md](KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md) | Approved-content architecture and the knowledge article inventory |

| [FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md) | Every item in this package with its approval status, owner and blocking effect |
| [IMPLEMENTATION-PHASES.md](IMPLEMENTATION-PHASES.md) | Proposed delivery phases and their entry and exit gates |
| [ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA.md](ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA.md) | Testable acceptance criteria for each phase |

## Status vocabulary

Every item in this package carries one of these labels. The register lists them all.

| Label | Meaning | May a partner use it? |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED` | The wording or figure is already published on the public site from a founder-maintained source in the repository (for example `web/src/lib/published-starting-prices.ts` or `web/src/lib/faq-library.ts`). Empower restates it; it does not create it. | Only once an Academy or resource version containing it is approved and published |
| `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED, OWNER REVIEW` | Published, but the source marks it `ownerReview: true`, so founders should confirm it before it is expanded | No, until confirmed |
| `CONFIRMED: SYSTEM BEHAVIOUR` | A fact about how the software behaves, verified in B0 source. It is not commercial approval | Not on its own |
| `PROPOSED POLICY` | A commercial or legal position that exists in B0 drafts or the draft `/partners` page but is not approved (for example the 30% acquisition commission) | No. Must always be labelled as proposed |
| `DRAFT` | Written in this package. Needs founder review | No |
| `FOUNDER DECISION` | Content cannot be finalised until a founder or adviser decides | No |
| `BLOCKED` | Waiting on an external prerequisite, such as the B0 merge or legal advice | No |

No item in this package is `APPROVED`. That status exists only in the future publishing workflow (see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)), where a founder records it against an immutable content version.

## Content rules applied throughout

These rules come from the B0 programme sources and the public-site content policy. They apply to every draft here and to every future edit.

1. **No guaranteed outcomes.** No ranking, traffic, enquiry, revenue or earnings guarantees. The source position is published at `faq-library.ts` (`ranking-guarantees`) and on `/partners` ("No guaranteed earnings").
2. **No invented proof.** No testimonials, quotes, statistics or client names beyond the published work listed in `web/src/lib/data.ts`. Partner reuse of published case studies still needs founder permission (see [CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](../intelligence/CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md)).
3. **Prices are the published starting prices only**: website from £2,000, Growth Partnership from £350 per month, Business Growth Audit £395, business email from £15 per month. Always paired with the starting-price boundary (`STARTING_PRICE_BOUNDARY`). GBP only.
4. **Commission and rewards are proposed, never promised.** Figures in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts` are illustrations of the proposed programme. Every plan is disabled by default and no reward is payable.
5. **Independence is preserved.** The Academy is optional and voluntary, as the programme states. No course is compulsory and no completion affects commission, allocation or standing. An employment solicitor should confirm this (register item `AP-GOV-02`).
6. **Partner-only and client-facing material are kept apart.** Client-facing material never contains commission, founder-only or internal information.
7. **Escalate rather than improvise.** Where an answer depends on scope, contract or technical review, the content says so and names the escalation route.

## Relationship to existing registers

This package extends, and does not replace, the B0 registers:

- [FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md](../intelligence/FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md): commercial, legal and operational decisions;
- [CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](../intelligence/CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md): content not yet written (much of which this package now drafts);
- [COMMERCIAL-ACTIVATION-GATES.md](../hardening/COMMERCIAL-ACTIVATION-GATES.md): release modes and gates.

When the founders approve an Empower item, record it in [FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md) and, where it resolves a row there, in the matching B0 register.
# Platform audit: reusable systems for Empower

**Status: DRAFT.** Audited against B0 head `4e713e5` (branch `claude/modest-newton-jo2d95`). Facts below are `CONFIRMED: SYSTEM BEHAVIOUR` unless marked otherwise. Anything not inspected is marked "not verified".

## Summary

The B0 Partner Portal already has the essential primitives for a Resource Centre: a versioned, immutable, audience-tagged resource table with a database-enforced publication lifecycle, a founder publishing form, a partner search box and an onboarding toolkit item reserved for the Academy. What is missing is structure (courses, lessons, knowledge articles with fields), approval evidence (who approved which version, and when it must be reviewed again), progress tracking and a proper search index. Empower should **extend these patterns, not replace them**.

## 1. Partner Portal (admin app, `/partner`)

| Aspect | Finding | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Location | Lives on the existing admin origin. No separate subdomain or authentication stack | `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts` (`partnerLoginUrl`), `admin/src/app/partner/page.tsx` |
| Role | `independent_partner` holds exactly one capability, `expansion.partner` | `admin/src/lib/rbac.ts:28` |
| Route guard | `/partner` and `/partner/*` map to `expansion.partner`; `/api/partner*` is the only API family that capability reaches | `admin/src/lib/rbac.ts:53`, `:99` |
| Workspace | One client component with tabs: Overview, Prospects & scope, Resource library, Commission centre, Achievements, My web page, Referrals, Onboarding, Meetings | `admin/src/components/expansion/ExpansionWorkspace.tsx:67` |
| Styling | Scoped `ex-*` classes in `expansion.css`: panels, badges, `details`-based resource rows, list rows | `admin/src/components/expansion/expansion.css` |
| Server guard | Partner reads run in a transaction behind `requireCapability("expansion.partner")` and `partnerGuard`, which share-locks the user row | `admin/src/lib/server/expansion-operations.ts:31-52` |

**Reuse:** add Academy and Resource Centre as new workspace areas (or child routes under `/partner`) behind the same capability. **Gap:** the workspace is a single large component; new areas should be separate route segments so they can be code-split and tested independently (see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)).

## 2. Founder administration (`/expansion`)

- Route `/expansion` requires `expansion.manage`; founder-only actions use `expansion.founder`. Owner and administrator roles exclude `expansion.partner`, so a founder account never doubles as a partner (`admin/src/lib/rbac.ts:26-27`).

# Operation Empower: B1 planning package

**Package status: DRAFT. Nothing in this folder is approved, published or available to partners or clients.**

Operation Empower prepares two partner capabilities for engineering:

- the **Partner Academy**, an optional, voluntary learning area inside the Partner Portal; and
- the **Sales Resource Centre**, an approved-content library and knowledge base that partners search before speaking to a prospect.

This is B1 research, architecture and content design only. It changes no application code, migrations, authentication, CI or production systems. Implementation must not start until B0 ([PR #155](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/155), branch `claude/modest-newton-jo2d95`) is merged. Its readiness record is [B0-MERGE-READINESS.md](../intelligence/B0-MERGE-READINESS.md).

## Status vocabulary

Every item in this package carries one of these labels. The register lists them all.

| Label | Meaning | May a partner use it? |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED` | The wording or figure is already published on the public site from a founder-maintained source in the repository (for example `web/src/lib/published-starting-prices.ts` or `web/src/lib/faq-library.ts`). Empower restates it; it does not create it. | Only once an Academy or resource version containing it is approved and published |
| `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED, OWNER REVIEW` | Published, but the source marks it `ownerReview: true`, so founders should confirm it before it is expanded | No, until confirmed |
| `CONFIRMED: SYSTEM BEHAVIOUR` | A fact about how the software behaves, verified in B0 source. It is not commercial approval | Not on its own |
| `PROPOSED POLICY` | A commercial or legal position that exists in B0 drafts or the draft `/partners` page but is not approved (for example the 30% acquisition commission) | No. Must always be labelled as proposed |
| `DRAFT` | Written in this package. Needs founder review | No |
| `FOUNDER DECISION` | Content cannot be finalised until a founder or adviser decides | No |
| `BLOCKED` | Waiting on an external prerequisite, such as the B0 merge or legal advice | No |

No item in this package is `APPROVED`. That status exists only in the future publishing workflow (see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)), where a founder records it against an immutable content version.

## Content rules applied throughout

These rules come from the B0 programme sources and the public-site content policy. They apply to every draft here and to every future edit.

1. **No guaranteed outcomes.** No ranking, traffic, enquiry, revenue or earnings guarantees. The source position is published at `faq-library.ts` (`ranking-guarantees`) and on `/partners` ("No guaranteed earnings").
2. **No invented proof.** No testimonials, quotes, statistics or client names beyond the published work listed in `web/src/lib/data.ts`. Partner reuse of published case studies still needs founder permission (see [CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](../intelligence/CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md)).
3. **Prices are the published starting prices only**: website from £2,000, Growth Partnership from £350 per month, Business Growth Audit £395, business email from £15 per month. Always paired with the starting-price boundary (`STARTING_PRICE_BOUNDARY`). GBP only.
4. **Commission and rewards are proposed, never promised.** Figures in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts` are illustrations of the proposed programme. Every plan is disabled by default and no reward is payable.
5. **Independence is preserved.** The Academy is optional and voluntary, as the programme states. No course is compulsory and no completion affects commission, allocation or standing. An employment solicitor should confirm this (register item `AP-GOV-02`).
6. **Partner-only and client-facing material are kept apart.** Client-facing material never contains commission, founder-only or internal information.
7. **Escalate rather than improvise.** Where an answer depends on scope, contract or technical review, the content says so and names the escalation route.

**Reuse:** Academy content may describe what was built (as the FAQ library already does). It must not quote outcomes, metrics or testimonials unless the claim is verified in that registry **and** founders approve partner use (register item `AP-PROOF-01`). The claim-selection pattern (permitted placement, review expiry) is the model for the knowledge base approval fields.

## 9. Public programme pages (`web/src/app/partners`)

- `/partners` presents the programme with an earnings calculator and the `FEATURE_AVAILABILITY` table, which already lists "Partner Academy: IN DEVELOPMENT, Optional and voluntary" and "Website Intelligence, Sales Studio, Ask ScaleSmiths: IN DEVELOPMENT, not yet available to partners".
- Its wording on independence ("an independent, commission-only opportunity. There is no salary, guaranteed income, compulsory working hours or sales target") is the source for the Professional Conduct course. The page itself is "Draft, built, not approved".
- Public partner profiles are off unless `PUBLIC_PARTNER_PROFILES_ENABLED=true` (`web/src/lib/partner-profile-public.ts:13`).

**Implication:** nothing in Empower changes the public page. If the Academy ships, the availability label changes only by a separate founder-approved content change.

## 10. Design systems

There are two token sets, both dark-first with gold accents:

| Token | Public site (`web/src/app/globals.css`) | Admin and portal (`admin/src/app/globals.css`) |
|---|---|---|
| Background | `--bg #0b0a08` (warm black) | `--bg #131416` (cool charcoal) |
| Surfaces | `--s1 #141210`, `--s2 #1c1915`, `--s3 #26221c` | `--s1 #1a1b1e`, `--s2 #222428`, `--s3 #2a2d31` |
| Text | `--t1 #f5efe6`, `--t2 #c9bdb0`, `--t3 #95887a` | `--t1 #f1f5f9`, `--t2 #a6b0be`, `--t3 #667085` |
| Accent | `--acc #e8a045` (amber gold) | `--acc #d1b266` (metallic gold) |
| Silver | `--silver #cfc7bc` | none |
| Display type | Syne (self-hosted) | Arial Black fallback under the `--font-syne` name |
| Body type | Inter | Inter |

The Partner Portal also hard-codes some values in `expansion.css` (`#131416`, `#18191b`, `#c3a86c`). [DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md](DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md) reconciles these and records a contrast finding: admin `--t3 #667085` is 3.71:1 on `--bg`, below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 threshold for body text.

## 11. Things Empower must not reuse

- **`delivery_resources` in the client portal** (`web/src/lib/schema.ts:223`) belongs to client project delivery. It is tenant-scoped client data and must stay separate from partner content.

- **AI features.** No AI provider, budget or data-processing agreement is approved ([FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md](../intelligence/FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md)). "Ask ScaleSmiths" stays out of scope; see the deterministic search decision in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md).

# Empower architecture (proposed)

**Status: DRAFT.** This is a design proposal for engineering review after B0 merges. No table, route or migration described here exists. Migration numbers are not reserved.

## 1. Goals and non-goals

**Goals**

1. Partners can find approved answers, resources and training quickly, and can tell at a glance what is approved, for whom, and until when.
2. Founders can draft, review, approve, publish, supersede and retire every content item, with evidence and an audit trail.
3. Partner-only and client-facing material can never be confused or cross-published by accident.
4. The Academy is optional and voluntary, and progress never affects commission, allocation, recognition or standing.

**Non-goals for B1 and the first build**

- No AI generation, AI answers, embeddings or paid AI APIs.
- No assessment that gates anything, no certification, no leaderboard.
- No file uploads, video hosting or third-party learning platform.
- No change to commission, markets, exclusivity or any B0 financial path.
- No client portal delivery of client-facing resources (a later, separate decision).

## 2. Building blocks

```
            Founder administration (/expansion → Content)                Partner Portal (/partner)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Draft editor → Review → Approve → Publish        │      │ Academy   Resources   Knowledge search  │
  │ Supersede / Archive / Review-due queue           │      │ Objection workspace   My progress       │
  └───────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘      └───────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                  │ expansion.founder (writes)                                  │ expansion.partner (reads)
                  ▼                                                             ▼
        content service (server only)  ──────────── published, partner-audience, in-review-window rows only
                  │
                  ▼
  PostgreSQL: content_items · content_versions · content_approvals · content_links
              academy_courses · academy_modules · academy_lessons · academy_progress
              knowledge_entries · search documents (tsvector)
```

All reads and writes go through server functions in the admin app, following the existing `requireCapability` and `partnerGuard` pattern in `admin/src/lib/server/expansion-operations.ts`. There is no client-supplied filter on audience or status.

## 3. Proposed data model

The model generalises `expansion_resources` (immutable versions, database-enforced lifecycle) and adds approval evidence modelled on the public-claims registry (`verifiedAt`, `reviewExpiresAt`, permitted placement).

### 3.1 Content families and versions

| Table | Purpose | Key columns |
|---|---|---|
| `empower_content_items` | A stable identity for one piece of content across versions (for example "Objection: too expensive") | `id`, `kind ∈ {resource, lesson, knowledge, objection, template}`, `slug` (unique), `audience ∈ {partner_only, client_facing}`, `owner_role`, `created_at` |
| `empower_content_versions` | Immutable content. Never updated except `status`; never deleted | `id`, `item_id`, `version` (unique per item), `title`, `body` (restricted Markdown), `fields jsonb` (kind-specific, validated), `source_refs jsonb` (list of repository paths or approved documents), `status ∈ {draft, in_review, approved, published, superseded, archived}`, `created_by`, `created_at` |
| `empower_content_approvals` | Append-only approval evidence | `id`, `version_id`, `decision ∈ {approved, changes_requested, rejected}`, `decided_by`, `decided_at`, `reference` (founder decision reference), `review_by date`, `notes` |
| `empower_content_links` | Typed relationships | `from_item`, `to_item`, `relation ∈ {supports_lesson, see_also, escalates_to, replaces}` |

Lifecycle, enforced by a trigger like `expansion_resource_lifecycle`:

```
draft ──► in_review ──► approved ──► published ──► superseded
  │           │                         │
  └──► archived ◄──────── changes ──────┴──► archived
```

- `in_review → approved` requires an `empower_content_approvals` row with `decision='approved'` by a user holding `expansion.founder`, and it must be a **different** founder from the version's author when two founders are active (founder decision `AP-GOV-04`).
- `approved → published` is a separate action, so approval and release can be scheduled apart.
- Publishing version N of an item moves the previously published version to `superseded` in the same transaction. There is at most one published version per item (partial unique index).
- A published version whose `review_by` date has passed is **not served to partners** (fail closed) and appears in the founder "review due" queue. This mirrors `reviewExpiresAt` in `web/src/lib/public-claims.ts`.
- `audience` belongs to the item, not the version, so a new version cannot quietly change who sees it. Changing audience means creating a new item.

### 3.2 Academy

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `empower_courses` | Course identity, order, summary, `content_item_id` for its description |
| `empower_modules` | Ordered modules within a course |
| `empower_lessons` | Ordered lessons; each points at a lesson `content_item` (so lesson text uses the same versioning and approval) |
| `empower_knowledge_checks` | Optional questions per lesson, stored in the lesson version's `fields` |
| `empower_progress` | `partner_id`, `lesson_item_id`, `version_id` read, `opened_at`, `completed_at`, `check_attempted bool` |

Rules:

- **Progress is private to the partner** and visible to founders only in aggregate (counts per course), unless the partner chooses to share it (founder decision `AP-GOV-03`). Progress has no foreign key to, or query from, any commission, allocation, recognition or achievement table, matching the meetings design in [PARTNER-OPERATIONS.md](../intelligence/PARTNER-OPERATIONS.md).
- Knowledge-check answers are not stored, only "attempted". No score is persisted.
- When a lesson is superseded, progress stays attached to the version that was read, and the lesson shows "updated since you read it".

### 3.3 Knowledge entries

A knowledge entry is a `content_item` of kind `knowledge`. Its version `fields` hold the required structure from [KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md](KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md):

```json
{
  "question": "string",
  "answer": "string (partner-facing, precise)",
  "client_explanation": "string (safe to say to a client)",
  "sources": ["web/src/lib/faq-library.ts#hosting-provided"],
  "limitations": "string",
  "escalation": { "required": "always | when | never", "condition": "string", "route": "technical_scoping | commercial_assistance | escalation | …" },
  "aliases": ["other ways people ask it"],
  "topic": "hosting"
}
```

The service validates the shape on write. A knowledge version without a source, limitation or escalation rule cannot move to `in_review`.

## 4. Search: deterministic first

**Recommendation: PostgreSQL full-text search with curated synonyms and exact alias matching. No embeddings, no language model.**

Why:

- Every answer a partner sees must be approved text. Retrieval that returns approved items verbatim is auditable; generated answers are not.
- No AI provider, budget or data-processing agreement is approved ([FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md](../intelligence/FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md)).
- The corpus is small (hundreds of items). PostgreSQL search is fast at that size, already in the stack, and adds no dependency.
- Results are reproducible, so they can be tested.

Design:

1. On publish, the service writes a search document for the version: `setweight(to_tsvector('english', title || question), 'A') || setweight(to_tsvector('english', aliases), 'A') || setweight(to_tsvector('english', answer || body), 'B') || setweight(to_tsvector('english', topic), 'C')`. A generated column or a row written in the same transaction keeps it consistent.
2. A founder-managed synonym list (`empower_search_synonyms`: term → canonical term, for example "ssl" → "https certificate", "aeo" → "ai search", "wp" → "wordpress") expands the query before `websearch_to_tsquery`. This is deterministic and reviewable.
3. Ranking: exact alias match first, then `ts_rank_cd` with weights, then topic order. Ties broken by slug, so ordering is stable.
4. Filtering in SQL, never in the browser: `status='published' AND review_by >= current_date AND audience` permitted for the caller.
5. Zero-result queries are logged (query text only, partner id hashed) so founders can see gaps and add aliases. Retention for this log is a founder decision (`AP-PRIV-02`).
6. Optional later step: `pg_trgm` for typo tolerance. It is still deterministic.

What would justify revisiting: a corpus of thousands of items, evidence from zero-result logs that synonyms cannot keep up, and an approved AI provider and data-processing agreement. Even then, the answer shown should be an approved entry, with retrieval-only assistance.

## 5. Rendering

- Bodies are a **restricted Markdown subset**: headings, paragraphs, lists, emphasis, tables, block quotes and links to internal routes or approved external domains. Raw HTML is disabled. Rendering happens on the server, with a sanitising pass as defence in depth.
- Client-facing items render with a visible "Client-facing: approved for sharing" ribbon. Partner-only items render with "Partner only: do not share".
- Every rendered item shows version, approval date and review-by date.
- Copy-to-clipboard is offered only for client-facing items and templates.

## 6. Integration with B0

| B0 system | Integration |
|---|---|
| `expansion_resources` | Keep as is. Migrate existing published rows into `empower_content_items` as `kind='resource'` in Phase 1, or leave them read-only and stop creating new ones. Decision `AP-ENG-01` |
| Onboarding toolkit | Link published handbook, brochure, pricing and commission references to `brochures`, `pricing_documents`, `commission_documents` and `academy` items. Requires the toolkit join to accept Empower items (small change) or the content to remain mirrored in `expansion_resources` |
| Meetings | Every escalation rule names a meeting type. "Request help" in the knowledge viewer opens the existing meeting request form pre-filled with the type and a reference to the entry |
| Audit | Every content write calls the existing `audit()` helper with an `empower_*` event name |
| RBAC | No new role. Reads: `expansion.partner`. Writes and approvals: `expansion.founder`. Founder preview uses the partner renderer with a "preview" banner |
| `partner-programme.ts` | Commercial lessons and the commission reference embed figures by **reference** to the programme constants, rendered with the plan version they come from, so they cannot drift from the engine |

## 7. Feature flags

Following the B0 pattern (everything defaults off):

| Flag | Default | Gates |
|---|---|---|
| `PARTNER_RESOURCE_CENTRE_ENABLED` | `false` | Partner-side Resource Centre and knowledge search |
| `PARTNER_ACADEMY_ENABLED` | `false` | Partner-side Academy |
| `EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED` | `false` in production until Phase 1 is accepted | Founder content workspace |

With a flag off, partner routes return 404 and the tab is hidden. The founder workspace can be enabled first so content can be loaded and approved before partners see anything.

## 8. Open engineering decisions

| ID | Question | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| `AP-ENG-01` | Migrate or freeze `expansion_resources` | Freeze: keep it for toolkit links, create new content in Empower tables, add a read adapter |
| `AP-ENG-02` | Markdown renderer | A small, maintained renderer with HTML disabled; justify the dependency in the PR |
| `AP-ENG-03` | Separate routes or tabs | Separate route segments under `/partner/academy`, `/partner/resources` and `/partner/knowledge`, sharing the portal shell |
| `AP-ENG-04` | Content seeding | A reviewed seed script that loads drafts from this folder as `draft` versions only, never as published |
# Empower security model (proposed)

**Status: DRAFT.** Extends [../SECURITY-MODEL.md](../SECURITY-MODEL.md) and the B0 hardening work. Nothing here changes authentication.

## 1. Assets

| Asset | Sensitivity | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Partner-only content (commission references, objection playbooks, escalation routes) | Internal | Leakage could be read as a commercial offer or misused by competitors |
| Client-facing content | Low once approved; high while draft | A leaked draft could be presented to a client as approved |
| Approval records | Integrity-critical | They are the evidence that content was approved |
| Partner progress | Personal data | Could be used to monitor or direct partners, which bears on independent status |
| Search logs | Personal data (low) | Reveal what an individual partner is working on |

## 2. Roles and capabilities

No new role or capability is required.

| Actor | Capability | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|---|
| Independent partner | `expansion.partner` | Read published, in-review-window content for their audience; search; record own progress; request a meeting from an entry | See drafts, approvals, other partners' progress, founder notes or search logs; write content |
| Founder | `expansion.manage` + `expansion.founder` | Draft, review, approve, publish, supersede, archive; see aggregate progress; preview as partner | Approve their own draft when two founders are active (decision `AP-GOV-04`); delete versions |
| Owner, administrator | per `admin/src/lib/rbac.ts` | Whatever their existing capabilities allow | They never hold `expansion.partner`, so they cannot act as a partner |
| Anonymous | none | Nothing | Reach any Empower route (the admin origin requires sign-in) |

## 3. Controls

### 3.1 Audience separation

- Audience is set on the **item**, cannot change, and is checked in SQL on every read.
- Partner-only items carry a "Partner only: do not share" ribbon and no copy button. Client-facing items carry an approval ribbon with the version and date.
- A lint rule in the content service refuses to move a `client_facing` version to `in_review` if its body contains blocked terms (commission, basis points, payout, withdrawal, referral reward, founder-only, internal) unless a founder explicitly overrides with a reason. This is a safety net, not a guarantee.

### 3.2 Publication integrity

- Immutable versions, enforced by a trigger (same approach as `expansion_resource_lifecycle`).
- Approval is a separate, append-only row recorded by a founder, with a reference and a review-by date.
- Publication fails closed: an expired review date, a missing approval or a disabled flag means the item is not served.
- Every transition writes an audit row with the actor and the version id.

### 3.3 Rendering safety

- Restricted Markdown, raw HTML disabled, server-side rendering, then sanitising.
- Links are limited to internal routes and an allow-list of external domains (for example `ico.org.uk`, `gov.uk`). Founders manage the allow-list.
- No file uploads in this scope, so there is no malware-scanning or storage requirement. Photographs remain unsupported, as in B0.

### 3.4 Input handling

- Every write goes through the existing command endpoint pattern with length limits (B0 uses 200 for titles and 30,000 for content).
- `fields` JSON is validated against a schema per `kind` on the server.
- Search input is length-limited (200 characters), passed as a bound parameter to `websearch_to_tsquery`, and rate-limited per partner (the public site's `web/src/lib/rate-limit-policy.ts` is the model; an admin-side equivalent was not verified).

### 3.5 Independence and privacy

- Progress is private to the partner by default. Founders see aggregates only, unless the partner chooses to share (decision `AP-GOV-03`).
- No progress, completion or knowledge-check data is joined to commission, allocation, recognition or achievements. A test should assert that no such query exists.
- Knowledge-check answers are not stored.
- Search logs: query text and a hashed partner id, retained for a founder-approved period (decision `AP-PRIV-02`). The privacy notice must mention them (decision `AP-PRIV-01`).

## 4. Threats and mitigations

| Threat | Mitigation | Residual risk |
|---|---|---|
| A partner presents a draft as approved | Partners never receive drafts; every rendered item shows approval metadata | A partner could paraphrase from memory; covered by the Professional Conduct course and the partner agreement |
| Partner-only commission information reaches a client | Audience on item, lint check, ribbons, no copy button | A partner can still screenshot; agreement and training cover this |
| A stale price or policy is quoted | Review-by dates fail closed; commercial figures embedded by reference to programme constants | A partner may have saved an old copy; versions show "updated since" |
| A founder approves their own mistake | Second-founder approval rule; audit trail | Single-founder periods need an explicit override with a reason |
| Stored XSS through content | No raw HTML, server rendering, sanitiser, link allow-list | Renderer dependency must be kept patched |
| Progress used to direct or monitor partners | Private by default, no joins to commercial tables, voluntary framing | Requires founder discipline and solicitor review (`AP-GOV-02`) |
| Search probing reveals hidden content | Search runs only over published, permitted rows; zero results look the same whether content is hidden or absent | None identified |
| Enumeration of other partners' data | All partner queries keyed by the authenticated actor via `partnerGuard` | None identified |

## 5. Verification expected at implementation

- Service tests for every lifecycle transition, including refusals.
- Real-PostgreSQL tests for the trigger and the one-published-version index, as B0 does for its guards.
- Role tests: a partner cannot reach any founder content action; an owner cannot reach partner routes.
- A browser test that a partner sees no draft, no expired item and no client-facing copy control on partner-only items.
- A test asserting progress tables are not referenced by commercial queries.

- **Progress is private to the partner** and visible to founders only in aggregate (counts per course), unless the partner chooses to share it (founder decision `AP-GOV-03`). Progress has no foreign key to, or query from, any commission, allocation, recognition or achievement table, matching the meetings design in [PARTNER-OPERATIONS.md](../intelligence/PARTNER-OPERATIONS.md).
- Knowledge-check answers are not stored, only "attempted". No score is persisted.
- When a lesson is superseded, progress stays attached to the version that was read, and the lesson shows "updated since you read it".

### 3.3 Knowledge entries

A knowledge entry is a `content_item` of kind `knowledge`. Its version `fields` hold the required structure from [KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md](KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md):

```json
{
  "question": "string",
  "answer": "string (partner-facing, precise)",
  "client_explanation": "string (safe to say to a client)",
  "sources": ["web/src/lib/faq-library.ts#hosting-provided"],
  "limitations": "string",
  "escalation": { "required": "always | when | never", "condition": "string", "route": "technical_scoping | commercial_assistance | escalation | …" },
  "aliases": ["other ways people ask it"],
  "topic": "hosting"
}
```

The service validates the shape on write. A knowledge version without a source, limitation or escalation rule cannot move to `in_review`.

## 4. Search: deterministic first

**Recommendation: PostgreSQL full-text search with curated synonyms and exact alias matching. No embeddings, no language model.**

Why:

- Every answer a partner sees must be approved text. Retrieval that returns approved items verbatim is auditable; generated answers are not.
- No AI provider, budget or data-processing agreement is approved ([FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md](../intelligence/FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md)).
- The corpus is small (hundreds of items). PostgreSQL search is fast at that size, already in the stack, and adds no dependency.
- Results are reproducible, so they can be tested.

Design:

1. On publish, the service writes a search document for the version: `setweight(to_tsvector('english', title || question), 'A') || setweight(to_tsvector('english', aliases), 'A') || setweight(to_tsvector('english', answer || body), 'B') || setweight(to_tsvector('english', topic), 'C')`. A generated column or a row written in the same transaction keeps it consistent.
2. A founder-managed synonym list (`empower_search_synonyms`: term → canonical term, for example "ssl" → "https certificate", "aeo" → "ai search", "wp" → "wordpress") expands the query before `websearch_to_tsquery`. This is deterministic and reviewable.
3. Ranking: exact alias match first, then `ts_rank_cd` with weights, then topic order. Ties broken by slug, so ordering is stable.
4. Filtering in SQL, never in the browser: `status='published' AND review_by >= current_date AND audience` permitted for the caller.
5. Zero-result queries are logged (query text only, partner id hashed) so founders can see gaps and add aliases. Retention for this log is a founder decision (`AP-PRIV-02`).
6. Optional later step: `pg_trgm` for typo tolerance. It is still deterministic.

What would justify revisiting: a corpus of thousands of items, evidence from zero-result logs that synonyms cannot keep up, and an approved AI provider and data-processing agreement. Even then, the answer shown should be an approved entry, with retrieval-only assistance.

## 5. Rendering

- Bodies are a **restricted Markdown subset**: headings, paragraphs, lists, emphasis, tables, block quotes and links to internal routes or approved external domains. Raw HTML is disabled. Rendering happens on the server, with a sanitising pass as defence in depth.
- Client-facing items render with a visible "Client-facing: approved for sharing" ribbon. Partner-only items render with "Partner only: do not share".
- Every rendered item shows version, approval date and review-by date.
- Copy-to-clipboard is offered only for client-facing items and templates.

## 6. Integration with B0

| B0 system | Integration |
|---|---|
| `expansion_resources` | Keep as is. Migrate existing published rows into `empower_content_items` as `kind='resource'` in Phase 1, or leave them read-only and stop creating new ones. Decision `AP-ENG-01` |
| Onboarding toolkit | Link published handbook, brochure, pricing and commission references to `brochures`, `pricing_documents`, `commission_documents` and `academy` items. Requires the toolkit join to accept Empower items (small change) or the content to remain mirrored in `expansion_resources` |
| Meetings | Every escalation rule names a meeting type. "Request help" in the knowledge viewer opens the existing meeting request form pre-filled with the type and a reference to the entry |
| Audit | Every content write calls the existing `audit()` helper with an `empower_*` event name |
| RBAC | No new role. Reads: `expansion.partner`. Writes and approvals: `expansion.founder`. Founder preview uses the partner renderer with a "preview" banner |
| `partner-programme.ts` | Commercial lessons and the commission reference embed figures by **reference** to the programme constants, rendered with the plan version they come from, so they cannot drift from the engine |

## 7. Feature flags

Following the B0 pattern (everything defaults off):

| Flag | Default | Gates |
|---|---|---|
| `PARTNER_RESOURCE_CENTRE_ENABLED` | `false` | Partner-side Resource Centre and knowledge search |
| `PARTNER_ACADEMY_ENABLED` | `false` | Partner-side Academy |
| `EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED` | `false` in production until Phase 1 is accepted | Founder content workspace |

With a flag off, partner routes return 404 and the tab is hidden. The founder workspace can be enabled first so content can be loaded and approved before partners see anything.

## 8. Open engineering decisions

| ID | Question | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| `AP-ENG-01` | Migrate or freeze `expansion_resources` | Freeze: keep it for toolkit links, create new content in Empower tables, add a read adapter |
| `AP-ENG-02` | Markdown renderer | A small, maintained renderer with HTML disabled; justify the dependency in the PR |
| `AP-ENG-03` | Separate routes or tabs | Separate route segments under `/partner/academy`, `/partner/resources` and `/partner/knowledge`, sharing the portal shell |
| `AP-ENG-04` | Content seeding | A reviewed seed script that loads drafts from this folder as `draft` versions only, never as published |
# Empower security model (proposed)

**Status: DRAFT.** Extends [../SECURITY-MODEL.md](../SECURITY-MODEL.md) and the B0 hardening work. Nothing here changes authentication.

## 1. Assets

| Asset | Sensitivity | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Partner-only content (commission references, objection playbooks, escalation routes) | Internal | Leakage could be read as a commercial offer or misused by competitors |
| Client-facing content | Low once approved; high while draft | A leaked draft could be presented to a client as approved |
| Approval records | Integrity-critical | They are the evidence that content was approved |
| Partner progress | Personal data | Could be used to monitor or direct partners, which bears on independent status |
| Search logs | Personal data (low) | Reveal what an individual partner is working on |

## 2. Roles and capabilities

No new role or capability is required.

| Actor | Capability | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|---|
| Independent partner | `expansion.partner` | Read published, in-review-window content for their audience; search; record own progress; request a meeting from an entry | See drafts, approvals, other partners' progress, founder notes or search logs; write content |
| Founder | `expansion.manage` + `expansion.founder` | Draft, review, approve, publish, supersede, archive; see aggregate progress; preview as partner | Approve their own draft when two founders are active (decision `AP-GOV-04`); delete versions |
| Owner, administrator | per `admin/src/lib/rbac.ts` | Whatever their existing capabilities allow | They never hold `expansion.partner`, so they cannot act as a partner |
| Anonymous | none | Nothing | Reach any Empower route (the admin origin requires sign-in) |

## 3. Controls

### 3.1 Audience separation

- Audience is set on the **item**, cannot change, and is checked in SQL on every read.
- Partner-only items carry a "Partner only: do not share" ribbon and no copy button. Client-facing items carry an approval ribbon with the version and date.
- A lint rule in the content service refuses to move a `client_facing` version to `in_review` if its body contains blocked terms (commission, basis points, payout, withdrawal, referral reward, founder-only, internal) unless a founder explicitly overrides with a reason. This is a safety net, not a guarantee.

### 3.2 Publication integrity

- Immutable versions, enforced by a trigger (same approach as `expansion_resource_lifecycle`).
- Approval is a separate, append-only row recorded by a founder, with a reference and a review-by date.
- Publication fails closed: an expired review date, a missing approval or a disabled flag means the item is not served.
- Every transition writes an audit row with the actor and the version id.

### 3.3 Rendering safety

- Restricted Markdown, raw HTML disabled, server-side rendering, then sanitising.
- Links are limited to internal routes and an allow-list of external domains (for example `ico.org.uk`, `gov.uk`). Founders manage the allow-list.
- No file uploads in this scope, so there is no malware-scanning or storage requirement. Photographs remain unsupported, as in B0.

### 3.4 Input handling

- Every write goes through the existing command endpoint pattern with length limits (B0 uses 200 for titles and 30,000 for content).
- `fields` JSON is validated against a schema per `kind` on the server.
- Search input is length-limited (200 characters), passed as a bound parameter to `websearch_to_tsquery`, and rate-limited per partner (the public site's `web/src/lib/rate-limit-policy.ts` is the model; an admin-side equivalent was not verified).

### 3.5 Independence and privacy

- Progress is private to the partner by default. Founders see aggregates only, unless the partner chooses to share (decision `AP-GOV-03`).
- No progress, completion or knowledge-check data is joined to commission, allocation, recognition or achievements. A test should assert that no such query exists.
- Knowledge-check answers are not stored.
- Search logs: query text and a hashed partner id, retained for a founder-approved period (decision `AP-PRIV-02`). The privacy notice must mention them (decision `AP-PRIV-01`).

## 4. Threats and mitigations

| Threat | Mitigation | Residual risk |
|---|---|---|
| A partner presents a draft as approved | Partners never receive drafts; every rendered item shows approval metadata | A partner could paraphrase from memory; covered by the Professional Conduct course and the partner agreement |
| Partner-only commission information reaches a client | Audience on item, lint check, ribbons, no copy button | A partner can still screenshot; agreement and training cover this |
| A stale price or policy is quoted | Review-by dates fail closed; commercial figures embedded by reference to programme constants | A partner may have saved an old copy; versions show "updated since" |
| A founder approves their own mistake | Second-founder approval rule; audit trail | Single-founder periods need an explicit override with a reason |
| Stored XSS through content | No raw HTML, server rendering, sanitiser, link allow-list | Renderer dependency must be kept patched |
| Progress used to direct or monitor partners | Private by default, no joins to commercial tables, voluntary framing | Requires founder discipline and solicitor review (`AP-GOV-02`) |
| Search probing reveals hidden content | Search runs only over published, permitted rows; zero results look the same whether content is hidden or absent | None identified |
| Enumeration of other partners' data | All partner queries keyed by the authenticated actor via `partnerGuard` | None identified |

## 5. Verification expected at implementation

- Service tests for every lifecycle transition, including refusals.
- Real-PostgreSQL tests for the trigger and the one-published-version index, as B0 does for its guards.
- Role tests: a partner cannot reach any founder content action; an owner cannot reach partner routes.
- A browser test that a partner sees no draft, no expired item and no client-facing copy control on partner-only items.
- A test asserting progress tables are not referenced by commercial queries.

3	**Status: DRAFT. No course is approved, published or available.** Initial lesson content is in [LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md](LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md) (courses 1 to 6) and [LESSONS-PRACTICE.md](LESSONS-PRACTICE.md) (courses 7 to 13).
4	
5	## Principles
6	
7	- **Optional and voluntary.** The programme describes the Academy as optional and voluntary (`FEATURE_AVAILABILITY` in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`). There are no compulsory courses, deadlines, scores, certificates, rankings or completion targets, and completion never affects commission, allocation, recognition or standing. Wording is "you may find it useful", never "you must". Solicitor review: `AP-GOV-02`.
8	- **Approved sources only.** Each lesson lists its sources. Where a source is a draft or a proposal, the lesson says so in the text.
9	- **Teach the boundary, not just the pitch.** Each service course has a lesson on what the service is *not*, and when to escalate.
10	- **Short lessons.** Five to ten minutes each, readable on a phone.
11	- **Knowledge checks are optional self-checks.** Answers are shown immediately and nothing is stored except "attempted".

35	## C01 Welcome to ScaleSmiths

41	2. explain what an independent partner does and does not do;

# Partner Academy curriculum

**Status: DRAFT. No course is approved, published or available.** Initial lesson content is in [LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md](LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md) (courses 1 to 6) and [LESSONS-PRACTICE.md](LESSONS-PRACTICE.md) (courses 7 to 13).

## Principles

- **Optional and voluntary.** The programme describes the Academy as optional and voluntary (`FEATURE_AVAILABILITY` in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts`). There are no compulsory courses, deadlines, scores, certificates, rankings or completion targets, and completion never affects commission, allocation, recognition or standing. Wording is "you may find it useful", never "you must". Solicitor review: `AP-GOV-02`.
- **Approved sources only.** Each lesson lists its sources. Where a source is a draft or a proposal, the lesson says so in the text.
- **Teach the boundary, not just the pitch.** Each service course has a lesson on what the service is *not*, and when to escalate.
- **Short lessons.** Five to ten minutes each, readable on a phone.
- **Knowledge checks are optional self-checks.** Answers are shown immediately and nothing is stored except "attempted".

## Course map

| # | Course | Modules | Lessons | Audience of content | Review owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C01 | Welcome to ScaleSmiths | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C02 | Professional Website Development | 3 | 8 | Partner only (includes client-safe phrasing) | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C03 | SEO and Digital Growth | 3 | 8 | Partner only | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C04 | Growth Partnerships | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C05 | Website Migration | 2 | 6 | Partner only | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C06 | Bespoke Software and Automation | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Delivery founder | `DRAFT` |
| C07 | Finding Prospects | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Founders + privacy adviser | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED` (marketing process) |
| C08 | Discovery Meetings | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C09 | Presenting ScaleSmiths | 3 | 6 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C10 | Objection Handling | 3 | 8 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |
| C11 | Commercial Policies | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Founders + accountant + solicitor | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED` (agreement, terms) |
| C12 | Professional Conduct | 3 | 7 | Partner only | Founders + employment solicitor | `DRAFT`, `BLOCKED` (agreement) |
| C13 | Advanced and Enterprise Opportunities | 3 | 6 | Partner only | Both founders | `DRAFT` |

Suggested (not required) order: C01, C12, C02, C04, C08, then any.

---

## C01 Welcome to ScaleSmiths

**Purpose:** a clear, honest picture of who ScaleSmiths is, what it sells and how the partnership works.

**Learning objectives.** After this course a partner can:
1. describe ScaleSmiths and its services in two sentences without overstating them;
2. explain what an independent partner does and does not do;
3. find approved answers in the Resource Centre and know when to ask for help;
4. tell the difference between approved, proposed and planned features.

**Modules and lessons**

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Who we are | C01-L1 The ScaleSmiths story in plain words | Based in Hucknall, Nottinghamshire; custom builds; published work; how to say it briefly |
| | C01-L2 What we sell | Four published offers plus independently scoped custom work; starting-price boundary |
| | C01-L3 How we work | Discovery, written proposal, phased delivery, evidence over promises |
| M2 Your role | C01-L4 What an independent partner does | Introduce, qualify, register, support; ScaleSmiths scopes, prices and delivers |
| | C01-L5 What is live, proposed and planned | Reading the availability labels; why nothing is promised |
| M3 Using the portal | C01-L6 Finding answers fast | Knowledge search, resources, approval ribbons, versions |
| | C01-L7 Getting help | Meeting types, escalation, what to send |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions (for example "A prospect asks whether we guarantee first place on Google. What is the approved answer?").

**Supporting resources:** [R01 Company brochure](resources/R01-company-brochure.md), [R02 Partner handbook](resources/R02-partner-handbook.md), knowledge entries `KB-COM-01`, `KB-ONB-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** confirm company description and service list (`AP-CNT-01`); confirm the partner role wording matches the final agreement (`AP-GOV-01`); confirm the availability labels at review time.

---

## C02 Professional Website Development

**Purpose:** explain ScaleSmiths website projects accurately and recognise a good-fit prospect.

**Learning objectives:**
1. explain what a typical website project includes and excludes;
2. state the published starting price with its boundary;
3. explain hosting, domains, ownership and self-editing at a client-friendly level;
4. recognise when a project is really custom software, e-commerce or migration and route it.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 The offer | C02-L1 What a website project includes | Messaging, structure, responsive build, search foundations, enquiry route, launch support |
| | C02-L2 What is separate | Hosting, ongoing SEO, content programmes, integrations, open-ended support |
| | C02-L3 Price and proposal | "From £2,000" and the starting-price boundary; the proposal is the scope |
| M2 Questions clients ask | C02-L4 Timelines | Confirmed after discovery; content readiness drives schedule |
| | C02-L5 Ownership and editing | Ownership follows signed documents and payment; editing is a scoping decision |
| | C02-L6 Technology and WordPress | Custom builds; WordPress is reviewed on its merits (owner review flag) |
| M3 Fit and routing | C02-L7 Good-fit signals | Established business, clear services, evidence to protect |
| | C02-L8 When it is not a standard website | E-commerce, booking, portals, migration → escalate |

**Optional knowledge check:** six questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R03 Website development guide](resources/R03-website-development-guide.md), [R11 Commercial pricing reference](resources/R11-commercial-pricing-reference.md), `KB-HOST-*`, `KB-DOM-*`, `KB-ECOM-01`, `KB-BOOK-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** confirm "what is included" list; confirm WordPress wording (source is `ownerReview`); approve use of published project names in partner conversations (`AP-PROOF-01`).

---

## C03 SEO and Digital Growth

**Purpose:** talk about search visibility, including AI search, accurately and without promises.

**Learning objectives:**
1. explain SEO, local SEO and technical SEO in plain language;
2. explain what is included in a build and what is ongoing work;
3. explain AI search (answer engines) honestly, without claiming control over it;
4. respond to "can you guarantee page one?" with the approved answer.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Foundations | C03-L1 What SEO is | Technical, content, on-page experience; ongoing work |
| | C03-L2 Local SEO | Area searches, consistent details, Google Business Profile, local proof |
| | C03-L3 Technical SEO | Crawl, render, canonicals, sitemaps, redirects, Core Web Vitals, HTTPS |
| M2 Honest expectations | C03-L4 Timescales and guarantees | Months, not weeks; no position is promised |
| | C03-L5 Build versus ongoing | Foundations in build; ongoing via project or Growth Partnership |
| | C03-L6 SEO and paid search | Different problems; honest recommendation |
| M3 AI search | C03-L7 What AI search and AEO mean | Answer engines, structured content, direct answers; no guarantee of inclusion |
| | C03-L8 Diagnosing "not on Google" | Indexing, intent mismatch, authority; why audits start in Search Console |

**Optional knowledge check:** six questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R06 SEO and AEO guide](resources/R06-seo-and-aeo-guide.md), `KB-SEO-*`, `KB-AIS-*`, `KB-ANL-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** approve the AI search lesson (no published FAQ answer exists yet; `AP-CNT-06`); confirm Business Growth Audit positioning.

---

## C04 Growth Partnerships

**Purpose:** explain the Growth Partnership as a scoped, ongoing service, not an unlimited retainer.

**Learning objectives:**
1. explain what a Growth Partnership can include and how scope is agreed;
2. state the published starting price and its boundary;
3. explain how requests are prioritised;
4. explain that it can follow a ScaleSmiths build or start with an existing site.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 The service | C04-L1 What a Growth Partnership is | SEO, conversion, content, analytics, automation, technical support; scoped |
| | C04-L2 What it is not | Not unlimited; not only maintenance; not a guarantee |
| | C04-L3 Price and term | From £350/month published; any minimum term is a proposal-level term (programme `standard-v2` twelve-month term is `PROPOSED POLICY`) |
| M2 How it runs | C04-L4 Roadmap and priorities | Agreed roadmap, incidents first, client portal requests |
| | C04-L5 Hosting, email and monitoring | Included only when the order says so |
| M3 Positioning | C04-L6 After a build | Launch as a measurement point |
| | C04-L7 Existing websites | Review before responsibility |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R04 Growth Partnership guide](resources/R04-growth-partnership-guide.md), `KB-HOST-02`, `KB-HOST-03`, `KB-ANL-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** decide whether a minimum term is offered to clients and how partners describe it (`AP-COM-03`); confirm suitability criteria for Growth-Partnership-only clients (B0 open decision).

---

## C05 Website Migration

**Purpose:** recognise migration opportunities and explain the risk honestly.

**Learning objectives:**
1. explain what a migration involves (platform, hosting, URLs, data);
2. explain how search risk is reduced and why it cannot be removed;
3. identify the information needed before a migration can be scoped;
4. escalate every migration for technical review.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Understanding migration | C05-L1 Types of migration | Platform rebuild, hosting move, domain change, CMS change |
| | C05-L2 WordPress and Shopify moves | Review what works first; Pinkys Prints as published example |
| | C05-L3 Redirects and search risk | URL mapping, metadata, internal links, post-launch indexing checks |
| M2 Preparing a referral | C05-L4 What to collect | Access, current URLs, analytics, integrations, licences |
| | C05-L5 Red flags | Unknown hosting, no access, expiring domain, unlicensed plugins |
| | C05-L6 Escalation | Always a technical scoping request |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R03 Website development guide](resources/R03-website-development-guide.md), [R10 Technical escalation guide](resources/R10-technical-escalation-guide.md), `KB-MIG-*`, `KB-RED-01`.

**Founder review requirements:** confirm migration wording (source `seo-rebuild` is `ownerReview`); approve the "red flags" list.

## C06 Bespoke Software and Automation

**Purpose:** spot genuine custom-software needs and avoid overselling them.

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R05 Bespoke software guide](resources/R05-bespoke-software-guide.md), `KB-CRM-01`, `KB-SW-*`, `KB-AUTO-01`.

## C10 Objection Handling

**Purpose:** respond to common concerns honestly, and know when the honest answer is "ScaleSmiths is not the right fit".

**Learning objectives:**
1. use the acknowledge, clarify, answer, confirm pattern;
2. respond to the eight most common objections with approved wording;
3. recognise objections that need escalation;
4. never resolve an objection with an unapproved discount or promise.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Method | C10-L1 The pattern | Acknowledge, clarify, answer, confirm |
| | C10-L2 When to stop | Poor fit, pressure, escalation |
| M2 Common objections | C10-L3 "It is too expensive" | Value, scope, audit, phases; no discounting |
| | C10-L4 "We already have a website or agency" | Review what works; audit as second opinion |
| | C10-L5 "Can you guarantee results?" | No guarantees; commitments to the work |
| | C10-L6 "We use WordPress, Wix or Shopify" | Not anti-platform; evidence first |
| | C10-L7 "We need to think about it" | Respect, summary, follow-up |
| M3 Practice | C10-L8 Using the objection workspace | Search, practise, copy client-safe lines |

**Optional knowledge check:** six scenario questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R08 Objection-handling playbook](resources/R08-objection-handling-playbook.md).

**Founder review requirements:** approve each objection response individually (`AP-OBJ-*`); confirm discounting rules (allowances are disabled; `AP-COM-05`).

---

## C11 Commercial Policies

**Purpose:** understand how pricing, payment and commission are *proposed* to work, and what is not yet decided.

**Status note:** `BLOCKED`. The partner agreement, twelve-month terms, payment schedules, refund treatment, withdrawal policy and VAT treatment are all open founder, accountant and solicitor decisions. This course must not be published before they are resolved. Every figure in it is `PROPOSED POLICY`.

**Learning objectives:**
1. distinguish published client prices from proposed partner terms;
2. explain at a high level how commission is proposed to be calculated on collected payments;
3. understand what is disabled or undecided;
4. never make a commercial commitment on ScaleSmiths' behalf.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Client pricing | C11-L1 Published starting prices | The four offers and the boundary |
| | C11-L2 Proposals and payment terms | Terms are per proposal; no blanket deposit policy |
| M2 Partner terms (proposed) | C11-L3 How commission is proposed to work | 30% on eligible collected payments; build plus first Growth Partnership payment |
| | C11-L4 Worked examples | £705 standard; discounted examples; bespoke |
| | C11-L5 What is not decided | Withdrawals, refunds, VAT, achievements, referrals |
| M3 Boundaries | C11-L6 What you may and may not agree | No pricing, discounts, terms or timelines |
| | C11-L7 Markets | No market is approved yet; GBP only |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R11 Commercial pricing reference](resources/R11-commercial-pricing-reference.md), [R12 Commission and payment reference](resources/R12-commission-and-payment-reference.md), `KB-TERMS-*`, `KB-PAY-*`, `KB-COMM-*`.

**Founder review requirements:** all items in [FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md](../intelligence/FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md) marked A or F that the course mentions; accountant review of every worked example; solicitor review of wording.

---

## C12 Professional Conduct

**Purpose:** protect clients, partners and ScaleSmiths through honest, lawful and respectful conduct.

**Status note:** `BLOCKED` on the final partner agreement. Wording on independent status must be reviewed by an employment solicitor.

**Learning objectives:**
1. describe the independent partner relationship accurately;
2. represent ScaleSmiths truthfully and within approved material;
3. handle personal data and confidential information properly;
4. handle complaints, conflicts and mistakes.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Your status | C12-L1 Independent, not employed | No salary, guaranteed income, compulsory hours or targets |
| | C12-L2 How to describe yourself | Approved titles; no implied employment, ownership or directorship |
| M2 Honesty | C12-L3 Truthful representation | Approved content only; no guarantees, invented proof or unapproved prices |
| | C12-L4 Pressure and vulnerability | No pressure selling; extra care with vulnerable people |
| M3 Information | C12-L5 Personal data | Collect only what is needed; portal not personal spreadsheets |
| | C12-L6 Confidentiality | Commission, exclusivity and founder information stay private |
| | C12-L7 Complaints and mistakes | Tell ScaleSmiths quickly; never cover up |

**Optional knowledge check:** five questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R02 Partner handbook](resources/R02-partner-handbook.md).

**Founder review requirements:** solicitor review of status wording (`AP-GOV-01`, `AP-GOV-02`); privacy adviser review of data handling (`AP-PRIV-01`); approved partner title wording (`AP-GOV-05`).

---

## C13 Advanced and Enterprise Opportunities

**Purpose:** recognise larger and more complex opportunities and bring ScaleSmiths in early.

**Learning objectives:**
1. recognise multi-site, established-organisation and platform opportunities;
2. understand that complex work is scoped after discovery and never sold against a starting price;
3. understand how additional business with an existing client is handled;
4. prepare a strong bespoke discovery request.

| Module | Lesson | Outline |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Recognising scale | C13-L1 Established business transformation | Multi-site, customer journeys, integrations |
| | C13-L2 Custom platforms and enterprise | Architecture, security, migrations, support |
| M2 How it is handled | C13-L3 Scoped after discovery | No starting price; written scope |
| | C13-L4 Existing clients and additional work | Additional-business claims, attribution evidence (proposed) |
| M3 Your part | C13-L5 Preparing a bespoke discovery request | Information to gather |
| | C13-L6 Joint meetings | When and how to request one |

**Optional knowledge check:** four questions.

**Supporting resources:** [R05 Bespoke software guide](resources/R05-bespoke-software-guide.md), [R10 Technical escalation guide](resources/R10-technical-escalation-guide.md).

**Founder review requirements:** attribution evidence standard (B0 open decision); bespoke eligibility; approve enterprise examples.
